instruction: Summarize how Maya's career direction changed from accepting the marketing role through the approved product transfer. Include the main turning points and their sources.

evidence.quote: I still don't know if marketing is for me
I'm finally enjoying the marketing work
I'm officially helping Sapna as a product associate
I've decided I want product
Maya's transfer to the product team is approved

reference_summary: Maya accepted a Marketing Associate role while still unsure whether marketing suited her. She enjoyed the work after settling in, then became more interested in product while building and revising Kids Spark. A 40 percent product allocation began on July 27. In September she decided to pursue product full time. Sapna supported the move but could not promise it; Pravin later supported it, and the transfer was approved for October 1.

instruction: Summarize how Maya adjusted to living and working in Bengaluru from May through June. Keep temporary feelings separate from later states.

evidence.quote: Better than I expected. The onboarding was useful
The hard part is coming back to an empty flat. I miss home and everyone from college
I've already been lonely here
I've started having lunch with the team

reference_summary: Maya's first week at work went better than expected, but she felt homesick and lonely in her flat during May. After Aryan declined to restart their relationship, she also struggled to focus for several days. By early June she felt more settled, spent time with colleagues, and began enjoying her marketing work. The May feelings were temporary states, not stable traits.

instruction: Summarize the Kids Spark project from Maya's first assignment through the revised flow and role allocation. Preserve the correction to how Pravin's first feedback was described.

evidence.quote: take a stretch project for Kids Spark
I presented the first Kids Spark flow on June 25
The learner path is strong for a first version
it was not a rejection of the project
40 percent of her time supporting Kids Spark as a product associate

reference_summary: Pravin assigned Maya the first Kids Spark concept and user flow in June, with Sapna guiding the product work. Maya presented it on June 25. She initially described Pravin's muted response as rejection, but Pravin later clarified that the positioning needed work and the project had not been rejected. Sapna gave specific revisions, Maya reworked the flow, and the July 22 review accepted it for testing. From July 27, Maya spent 40 percent of her time on Kids Spark as a Product Associate.

instruction: Summarize how Maya's working relationship with Pravin changed. Distinguish Maya's suspicions from what Pravin said and did.

evidence.quote: Pravin explains the work without making me feel silly for asking questions
it was not a rejection of the project
No. That's just how it feels
This is about campaign coverage, not your Kids Spark allocation
I will support the transfer

reference_summary: Maya first saw Pravin as patient and supportive. His response to her first Kids Spark presentation created tension, though he later said he had asked for clearer positioning rather than rejected the project. In August, Maya suspected he was resisting her move to product, but she said he had not given that reason; his leave email cited campaign coverage. After Maya explained her goal directly in September, Pravin said he understood and supported the transfer and handoff.

instruction: Summarize how Maya's workload and preference for product work changed from June through September. Include what was current at each stage.

evidence.quote: I'm finally enjoying the marketing work
I spent about two hours after work on it most evenings, but I wanted to keep going
40 percent of her time supporting Kids Spark as a product associate and 60 percent on marketing
I like product work, but I can't keep doing both this way
I've decided I want product

reference_summary: In June, Maya enjoyed marketing while taking on Kids Spark as a stretch project. In July, she spent extra evenings revising the product and wanted to continue; her official allocation became 40 percent product and 60 percent marketing. By August, demands from both teams left her exhausted even though she still liked product work. In September, she decided to move into product full time, and the company approved that change for October 1.
